title: A frog in the school pond
body: A student watched a frog in the school pond for a day. When the frog stayed fully under water for a long time, its nostrils were closed and its lungs were not in use, yet it stayed active and swam away when disturbed. Later, while it sat on a rock at the edge of the pond with its nostrils open, the floor of its mouth moved up and down rhythmically. The student noted that the frog's skin was always moist and slippery and that many fine blood vessels could be seen just beneath its surface. The teacher explained that a frog uses different respiratory surfaces depending on whether it is in water or on land.
